 JUDGMENT

This appeal under Section 19 (1) of the Family Courts Act, 1984, against the judgment dated 14.09.2016 passed in MC.No.649/2014 by the VI Additional Principal Judge, Bengaluru Family Court by which the petition filed by the appellant/wife seeking dissolution of marriage under Sections 13(1)(i)(ia), 25 and 27 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (for short 'the Act') was partly allowed.

entities.text: VI Additional Principal Judge, Bengaluru Family Court
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Facts giving rise to filing of the appeal in brief are, marriage between the parties was solemnized on 13.06.2003 at T. Narasipura in Mysore District as per the customs and out of the wedlock, there were no issues.

3. The appellant filed petition on 07.02.2014 seeking dissolution of marriage and for a direction to respondent/husband to return gold jewels, cash and other articles, which were given at the time of marriage and with a prayer seeking permanent alimony for future maintenance.

4. The appellant averred that she married first respondent/husband on 13.06.2003 and at the time of marriage, a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- was paid by her father to the first respondent, 90 grams gold jewels and silver articles were also given as per the demand of the first respondent.
As per the customs prevailing in the community, father of the appellant gave a cow to the first respondent.
Father of the appellant spent Rupees 5 to 6 lacs towards performance of the marriage.

First respondent belonged to landlord family having agricultural land and father of the first respondent Smt. Parvathi vs Sri. Nandeesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17202052/
2 was also an employee.

First respondent was involved in money lending business and the cash and jewels given at the time of marriage have been invested for the purpose of money lending business and further started demanding more money.
5. The appellant has averred that after the marriage first respondent and his parents started harassing the appellant and demanded more dowry.

It was averred that when the appellant was not well she was taken to hospital and thereafter, the father of the appellant took her along with him and thereafter for about three months the appellant stayed with her parents.

It was also averred that on 13.8.2004, the first respondent in a drunken state had come to her parental house and insisted the appellant to return to matrimonial home and he assured that he will take care of the appellant and would not harass her.
Accordingly, he took the appellant to the matrimonial home.
6. It was further averred that first respondent did not change his attitude, and again started ill treating the appellant.
He used to assault the appellant for no reason, which caused physical and mental torture to the appellant.
It was averred that on 24.08.2004, first respondent assaulted the appellant and caused bodily injury.
He had forcibly removed the mangalasutra and poured kerosene on her body and threatened to kill her and out of fear, the appellant left the matrimonial home.

It was pleaded that Appellant was treated in Bowring Hospital, Bangalore for the injuries sustained by her and from September 2004 the appellant is taking shelter in her parents' house without any means.

The father of the appellant lodged a dowry harassment complaint before the T. Narasipura Police Station on 06.11.2004.
7.
It was also pleaded that the first respondent husband filed M.C.No.1/2005 before the Court of Senior Civil Judge and JMFC at T.Narasipura seeking relief of restitution of conjugal rights.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and JMFC at T.Narasipura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The said petition came to be dismissed on 15.06.2013.

The first respondent is leading adulterous life with second respondent and having a child, hence the petition was filed seeking dissolution of marriage, permanent alimony and return of articles before the Family Court.
8. The first respondent entered appearance before the Family Court and filed objections.
The second respondent remained absent despite service of notice, hence was placed ex-parte before the Trial Court.
9. The first respondent opposed the petition by denying the averments of the petition.
The first respondent admitted that appellant is the legally wedded wife, however, he denies other averments of the petition.
It was averred that appellant has insisted the first respondent husband, to leave his native place and to reside with her at Bangalore city.
When the said demand was not acceded, she created nuisance and abruptly left the matrimonial home without any reason.

It was further pleaded that appellant has filed a false criminal case which is registered as Crime No.152/2004 for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 506 of IPC r/w Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
The appellant filed petition after a lapse of twelve years making bald allegations.
The first respondent has no personal income of his own and he is depending on meager income of his parents and the property bearing survey numbers 308 and 309 belongs to his mother.
He denied that he is running money lending business as alleged in the petition.
It was further averred that he has not married the second respondent as alleged in the petition and sought for dismissal of the petition.

3 10.
The Family Court recorded the evidence.
The appellant examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P1 to P11.
The first respondent has not adduced any evidence.

The Family Court vide judgment and decree dated 14.09.2016 partly allowed the petition of the appellant filed under Section 13 of the Act by dissolving the marriage solemnized between the appellant and first respondent on 13.06.2003 and directed first respondent to pay Rs.5,000/- as monthly maintenance from the date of petition till her life time and prayer with regard to return of cash, jewelry and permanent alimony has been rejected.
11.
We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the respondent.
Perused the material on record.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that present appeal is filed being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree dated 14.09.2016 insofar as rejection of appellants' prayer for return of cash, jewels and permanent alimony.

12. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that Family Court has failed to appreciate the fact that father of the appellant paid Rs.1,00,000/-, 90 grams gold jewels, silver articles and gave a cow as per the customs.
It was further contended that appellant's father has spent Rupees 5 to 6 lacs towards marriage as per the prevailing customs of the community.

It further submitted that despite meeting all the demands of first respondent and his family members, first respondent failed to perform his marital obligation and caused physical and mental torture to the appellant forced the appellant to leave the matrimonial home and join her parents, without any of her fault.

Despite placing sufficient material on record, the Trial Court has failed to appreciate the - 10 - same and has come to an erroneous conclusion and has rejected the appellant's claim for return of cash, jewels and also refused to grant permanent alimony.
It was further contended that grant of Rs.5,000/- per month maintenance to the appellant till her life time is very meager amount and requires to be enhanced by awarding permanent alimony.
13. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent reiterates the averments made in the statement of objections filed before the Family Court and seeks for dismissal of the appeal.
14. We have considered the submission of both the parties and perused the material on record.
Both the parties have not disputed the relationship between them.
The prayer in the appeal is restricted only with regard to return of cash, jewelry and grant of permanent alimony.
The Family Court awarded interim maintenance of Rs.5,000/- per month to the appellant on 18.11.2015 during the pendency of proceedings.
The said order has not been challenged by the first respondent.
The first respondent except filing statement of objections opposing the petition, had not chosen to adduce any evidence from his side and has not cross-examined PW.1.

In the absence of any challenge to the testimony of PW.1 by way of cross- examination, there is no ground to disbelieve the evidence of PW.1 and documentary evidence produced by her, which are marked as Smt. Parvathi vs Sri. Nandeesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17202052/
4 Exs.P1 to P11.
16.
The appellant has made specific averment in the petition and adduced oral evidence that the first respondent and his family members are having sufficient land.
It was also stated that the first respondent is doing money lending business and having sufficient income.

The Family Court has not accepted the said evidence only on the ground that - 12 - the appellant has failed to produce any material with regard to properties owned by the first respondent and not produced any evidence to show that he has sufficient income to award permanent alimony of Rs.20,00,000/-.

The Family Court came to the conclusion that there is lack of material evidence on record to prove that the gold jewels, cash and other articles were in the custody of the first respondent, hence, appellant is not entitled for the relief of return of ornaments and permanent alimony, but only for a monthly maintenance of Rs.5,000/-.
17.

On meticulous examination of pleading and evidence on record, it is apparent that appellant has specifically pleaded in para 13 of the petition that cash, gold jewelry and other articles have been given to first respondent and he has misappropriated the same and it was not returned to the appellant.
Annexure-A is the list enclosed along with the petition - 13 - specifying each of the jewelry articles etc., PW.1 in her examination in chief has reiterated the same.

18. On careful perusal of para 14 of the petition, appellant has specifically stated that first respondent belongs to landlord family and they have agricultural land at T.Narasipura and has furnished the particulars of the immovable properties.

The appellant in her pleading as well as evidence clearly stated that first respondent retained and misappropriated the cash, gold jewelry and silver articles, which are enumerated in the list furnished at Annexure-A.
In the absence of any contrary evidence, the Family Court ought not to have disbelieved the same.

On careful consideration of pleading and evidence on record and in the absence of any contrary evidence by first respondent, we have no hesitation to say that Trial Court has committed error in rejecting the prayer for return of cash, jewels and for permanent alimony.
It will be useful to refer to the decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of VIDHYADHAR Vs. MANIKRAO AND ANOTHER (1999) 3 SCC 573

has held at paragraph 17 as follows :-
"17.

Where a party to the suit does not appear in the witness-box and states his own case on oath and does not offer himself to be cross-examined by the other side, a presumption would arise that the case set up by him is not correct as has been held in a series of decisions passed by various High Courts and the Privy Council beginning Smt. Parvathi vs Sri. Nandeesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17202052/
5 from the decision in Sardar Gurbakhsh Singh v. Gurdial Singh.

entities.text: Sardar Gurbakhsh Singh v. Gurdial Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was followed by the Lahore High Court in Kirpa Singh v. Ajaipal Singh and the Bombay High Court in Martand Pandharinath Chaudhari v. Radhabai Krishnarao Deshmukh.

entities.text: Martand Pandharinath Chaudhari v. Radhabai Krishnarao Deshmukh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Madhya Pradesh High Court in Gulla Kharagjit Carpenter v. Narsingh Nandkishore Rawat also followed the Privy Council decision in Sardar Gurbakhsh Singh case.

entities.text: Gulla Kharagjit Carpenter v. Narsingh Nandkishore Rawat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The - 15 - Allahabad High Court in Arjun Singh v. Virendra Nath held that if a party abstains from entering the witness-box, it would give rise to an adverse inference against him.

Similarly, a Division Bench of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in Bhagwan Dass v. Bhishan Chand drew a presumption under Section 114 of the Evidence Act, 1872 against a party who did not enter the witness-box."

In the case of MUDDASANI VENKATA NARSAIAH (DEAD) THROUGH LEGAL REPRESENTATIVES Vs. MUDDASANI SAROJANA (2016) 12 SCC 288 has held at paragraph 15 as follows :-
"15.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, there was no effective cross- examination made on the plaintiff's witness with respect to factum of execution of sale deed, PW 1 and PW 2 have not been cross- examined as to factum of execution of sale deed.
The cross-examination is a matter of substance not of procedure one is required to put one's own version in cross-examination of opponent.
The effect of non-cross-examination - 16 - is that the statement of witness has not been disputed.

The effect of not cross-examining the witnesses has been considered by this Court in Bhoju Mandal v.
Debnath Bhagat.
This Court repelled a submission on the ground that the same was not put either to the witness or suggested before the courts below.
Party is required to put his version to the witness.

If no such questions are put the Court would presume that the witness account has been accepted as held in Chuni Lal Dwarka Nath v.
Hartford Fire Insurance Co.Ltd."
(Underlined portion - Emphasis applied by this Court)
20.

sentences.text: The finding of the Trial Court that the appellant has failed to produce material, is perverse and contrary to the evidence on record.

Insofar as grant of permanent alimony is concerned, this Court is required to take into account various factors like the status of the parties, age of the parties,
income and expenditure, the present day cost of living and also required to take into account the amount which would - 17 - Smt. Parvathi vs Sri. Nandeesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17202052/
6 be just, reasonable and realistic.

The Family Court has erred in fixing the Rs.5,000/- per month maintenance, which is unrealistic as the appellant is aged about 34 years and is dependent on her parents as she has no independent income and required to survive on the said amount for her life time.
Keeping in mind the realistic approach, we deem it just and proper to grant permanent alimony of Rs.8,00,000/- to the appellant.
In the absence of any contrary evidence, we direct the first respondent to return the cash, gold jewelry and other articles enumerated in Annexure-A to the petition or its value.

21. For the foresaid reasons, the impugned judgment dated 14.09.2016 passed in M.C.No.649/2014 is modified with a direction to the first respondent husband to return the articles listed at Annexure-A to the petition, if the articles are not available its value to be paid to the appellant and further directed to pay permanent alimony of - 18 - Rs.8,00,000/- in lieu of monthly maintenance of Rs.5,000/-.
22.
Ordered accordingly.
In the result, the appeal is partly allowed.
